'''Jayadev Siddhanta Athreya''' (born 1983<ref>{{Cite web |last=Congress |first=The Library of |title=Athreya, Jayadev S. - LC Linked Data Service: Authorities and Vocabularies {{!}} Library of Congress, from LC Linked Data Service: Authorities and Vocabularies (Library of Congress) |url=https://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/no2019173427.html |access-date=2026-04-15 |website=id.loc.gov}}</ref>) is a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Washington]]. He is a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]]. His research interests are in [[ergodic theory]], [[dynamical systems]], and [[geometry]].

== Education ==
Athreya grew up in [[Ames, Iowa]] where he obtained a Bachelor of Science at [[Iowa State University]] in 2000. He went on to earn a MS in 2001 and a PhD in 2006 both in mathematics at the [[University of Chicago]] where he was advised by [[Alex Eskin]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Athreya |first=Jayadev |date=July 2022 |title=JAYADEV SIDDHANTA ATHREYA CV |url=https://faculty.washington.edu/jathreya/CVJuly2022.pdf |access-date=15 April 2026 |website=faculty.washington.edu}}</ref>

== Career ==
After graduating Athreya was a postdoctoral fellow at [[Yale University]] and [[Princeton University]].  In 2006, he was at Yale. In 2007, he took on a position at Princeton for a year before returning back to be a Gibbs instructor at Yale.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Jayadev Athreya {{!}} PIMS - Pacific Institute for the Mathematical Sciences |url=https://www.pims.math.ca/profiles/jayadev-athreya |access-date=2026-04-15 |website=www.pims.math.ca}}</ref>

In 2010,  he started a position as assistant professor at the [[University of Illinois]] where he founded and directed the Illinois Geometry Lab, now known as the Illinois Mathematics Lab.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Illinois Mathematics Lab {{!}} Information and resources for current and potential members of the Illinois Geometry Lab {{!}} Department of Mathematics {{!}} Illinois |url=https://iml.math.illinois.edu/ |access-date=2026-04-15 |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2015, he went on to be an associate professor at the [[University of Washington]] and created the Washington Experimental Mathematics Lab.<ref>{{Cite web |title=WXML Team {{!}} WASHINGTON eXPERIMENTAL MATHEMATICS LAB |url=https://www.wxml.math.washington.edu/?page_id=57 |access-date=2026-04-15 |language=en}}</ref> In 2020, he was promoted to full professor at the University of Washington.<ref name=":0" />

In 2021, Athreya became Interim Director of the [[Pacific Institute for the Mathematical Sciences]] where in 2022 he took on the position of co-Director. Since 2021, Athreya still resides on the board of directors of the Pacific Institute for the Mathematical Sciences.<ref name=":1" />

==Awards and honors==
He was awarded a visiting fellowship by the London Mathematical Society in 2009.<ref name=":0" />

In 2025, Athreya became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web |title=AMS :: Fellows of the American Mathematical Society |url=https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows_by_year.cgi |website=www.ams.org |access-date=15 September 2025}}</ref>

== Social justice ==
{{Quote box
| quote = The activity of collaborating with the police is not something we feel a mathematician should be doing.
| author = Jayadev Athreya
| source = Nature
}}
In reaction to [[United States racial unrest (2020–2023)|recent killings]] of [[List of people killed during the 2020–23 United States racial unrest|individuals]] in 2020, Athreya and other mathematicians wrote a letter pleading for their peers to cease collaborations with [[police departments]] due to well documented disparities in how these agencies treated people of different races and ethnicities. More specifically, they criticized the practice of [[predictive policing]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Castelvecchi |first=Davide |date=2020-06-19 |title=Mathematicians urge colleagues to boycott police work in wake of killings |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-020-01874-9 |journal=Nature |language=en |doi=10.1038/d41586-020-01874-9|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In 2023, Athreya signed a letter in solidarity with the [[Haverford College|Haverford]] [[Faculty for Justice in Palestine]] as well as to sharing mourning over the killings of the students Kinnan Abdalhamid, Tahseen Ahmed, and Hisham Awartani in November of the same year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Palestine |first=Haverford Faculty for Justice in |date=2023-11-27 |title=Haverford Faculty for Justice in Palestine Releases Statement Supporting Pro-Palestinian Students |url=https://www.leftvoice.org/haverford-faculty-for-justice-in-palestine/ |access-date=2026-04-15 |website=Left Voice |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Research==
Athreya along with [[David Aulicino]] and Patrick Hooper discovered that there exists an infinite number of straight paths on the dodecahedron that start and end at one vertex without intersecting any other vertex.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Roberts |first1=Siobhan |title=A Mathematical 'Fever Dream' Hits the Road |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/03/14/science/mathematics-daubechies-mathemalchemy.html |access-date=15 September 2025 |work=New York Times |date=March 14, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Klarreich |first1=Erica |title=Mathematicians Report New Discovery About the Dodecahedron |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/mathematicians-report-new-discovery-about-the-dodecahedron-20200831/ |website=Quanta Magazine |access-date=15 September 2025 |language=en |date=31 August 2020}}</ref>
